recentItems.title: Belgrade residents on Kosovo ex-President Thaci being convicted of war crimes, sentenced to 25 years
recentItems.description:
(16 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY: 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Belgrade, Serbia - 16 September 2026
1. Various of people on street 
2. SOUNDBITE (Serbian) Dragan Tomovic, local resident:
”I think that’s not enough, not enough. He deserves a life sentence.” 
3. People on street 
4. SOUNDBITE (Serbian) Relja Janjic, local resident:
”I believe it is not enough having in mind what he did, but in any case, it means something for Serbian people.” 
5. People on street
6. SOUNDBITE (Serbian) Goran Simic, local resident:
”I think he could have got a higher sentence. I have not followed the trial in detail, but for what he is being accused of, he could have received higher sentence.” 
7. People on street 
STORYLINE:
Belgrade residents reacted as a European Union-backed court on Wednesday convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of four counts of war crimes committed during his country’s war for independence from Serbia and sentenced him to 25 years in prison.

Dragan Tomovic, a local to Belgrade, said 25 years was not enough. 

"He deserves a life sentence,” Tomovic remarked.

For Relja Janjic, the sentence may be short, but it still carries meaning. 

”I believe it is not enough having in mind what he did, but in any case, it means something for Serbian people,” he said. 

Thaci, who is 58, resigned from office nearly six years ago to face the charges. 

He was convicted by a panel of judges at the Kosovo Specialist Chambers of murder, torture, cruel treatment and arbitrary detention. 

He can appeal.

Thaci faced multiple counts of war crimes and crimes against humanity, including murder, torture and persecution alongside three other former Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) leaders who fought Serb forces in the 1998-99 war. 

They are widely regarded as national heroes in Kosovo.

The four were all acquitted on six charges of crimes against humanity because the judges said the prosecutors failed to prove that crimes were committed as part of a widespread and systematic attack on civilians. 

The prosecutors had asked for a maximum 45-year prison sentence for Thaci and the other defendants, Kadri Veseli, Rexhep Selimi and Jakup Krasniqi. 

All denied the charges against them. 

Veseli was sentenced to 18 years, Selimi to 13 years and Krasniqi to 25 years in prison. 

AP Video by Ivana Bzganovic.

recentItems.title: El tesoro de marionetas de animación de Aardman sale a subasta en Reino Unido
recentItems.description:
(16 Sep 2026) 
Reino Unido Marionetas Subasta SP 
Source: ASSOCIATED PRESS
No additional restrictions beyond those terms outlined in your license agreement.
Vídeo de AP realizado por Tom Rayner.
 
Sin restricciones adicionales más allá de los términos estipulados en su acuerdo de licencia
 
El tesoro de marionetas de animación de Aardman sale a subasta en Reino Unido
 
———————————————————————————————————————
ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Londres, Reino Unido - 10 de septiembre de 2026 
 
Un tesoro de marionetas de animación con los personajes más icónicos de Aardman sale a subasta para conmemorar el 50 aniversario del estudio británico.
 
El catálogo incluye más de 220 artículos que abarcan medio siglo de producciones realizadas por el estudio de Bristol.
 
Entre las piezas destacan las marionetas originales de ‘stop-motion’ —auténticas y verificadas— de Wallace, Gromit y el malvado Feathers McGraw. 
 
Todos los lotes parten de un precio inicial de 100 libras esterlinas.
 
SONIDO (inglés) Sian Taylor, gerente de subastas de Propstore:
“Asignaríamos una estimación de precio”, dijo esta gerente de subastas. “Nunca se ha hecho algo así, contar con una colección tan increíble proveniente directamente de Aardman”.
 
Will Becher, director y animador de Aardman, que trabajó en la película “Evasión en la granja” comentó:
 
SONIDO (inglés) Will Becher, director y animador, Aardman: 
“Este Wallace es increíblemente único”, Es la razón por la que está aquí a mi lado, porque solo existe uno como él,” dijo.
 
Además de las marionetas y el atrezo, se exhiben guiones gráficos de las distintas películas y obras de arte originales de Nick Park, el creador de Wallace y Gromit. 
 
Se espera que estas marionetas de arcilla alcancen precios de decenas de miles de libras, porque son “de alta tecnología” dice Becher
 
SONIDO (inglés) Will Becher, director y animador, Aardman;
“Sin embargo el vestuario está diseñado para parecer arcilla, aunque a menudo es de silicona; esto nos permite tener los distintos colores y también las texturas”, dijo. 
 
Los beneficios de la venta se destinarán directamente a programas de desarrollo de talento en todo el estudio; servirán para financiar becas en la academia Aardman y talleres de formación, así como para crear oportunidades para cineastas de animación emergentes. 
 
La subasta mundial en directo tendrá lugar el 24 de septiembre de 2026. 
 
ANNE MARIE GARCIA, ASSOCIATED PRESS

STORYLINE:
Los fanáticos de la animación de todo el mundo tienen una oportunidad única de adquirir una pieza de la historia del cine británico, ya que Aardman subasta más de 220 marionetas icónicas y objetos de recuerdo.

La venta coincide con el 50 aniversario del estudio y las ganancias serán reinvertidas en la formación de una nueva generación de animadores.

La subasta conmemora los 50 años del estudio británico y todos los lotes tienen una oferta inicial de 100 libras esterlinas.

Las pujas comenzaron oficialmente el 4 de septiembre y culminarán con una subasta global en vivo el 24 de septiembre de 2026.

El catálogo incluye más de 220 artículos de casi todas las producciones realizadas durante el medio siglo de historia del estudio de Bristol, lo que ofrece a los fanáticos una oportunidad única de poseer una pieza de la historia de la animación.

Entre las principales piezas de la subasta se encuentran las marionetas originales utilizadas en pantalla para la animación stop-motion de Wallace, Gromit y el villano Feathers McGraw —incluido su característico disfraz con guante rojo— de la película de 2024 “Vengeance Most Fowl”.



Video de AP por Tom Rayner

recentItems.title: inside Llewyn Davis cast and crew interviews
recentItems.description:
(6 Sep 2013) 

STORYLINE:
AP Entertainment
Cannes, France 20 May 2013
1. SOUNDBITE (English) T-Bone Burnett/Music Producer:
"Well lets see, I don't have a career, that's the... it's a funny thing, I've managed not to have a career, I just do what I do when I wake up in the morning every day and I've done it for 50 years almost now, 48 years, I just keep doing the same thing every morning. It's not like I can progress up a ladder or anything like that I just exist in my own little world, like we all do you know. I just try and do the very best work I can, that's really, really all I think about. I just want to make everything of the highest possible quality that I can and I want to make the best use of my time."
AP Entertainment
Cannes, France 20 May 2013
2. SOUNDBITE (English) Oscar Isaac, Actor - on when he first realized he could make a career in showbusiness:
"I guess when they started paying me. I mean really, it's like 'really? you want to pay me for this?' I'm like 'all right, it's your dollar.' So that did help me focus in on what I wanted to study I guess when I went to college because I was in bands and stuff and trying to open for Green Day at this festival or do that. And then when I started doing some professional theatre and I was like 'oh I can buy food, that's nice.' So then I went to go study acting and I kind of had to leave the band thing behind for a little while."
AP Entertainment
Cannes, France 20 May 2013
3. SOUNDBITE (English) Justin Timberlake, actor and Carey Mulligan, actress - on when they first realized they could make a career in showbusiness: 
Timberlake: "I just feel lucky because I'm not really good at... I wasn't really good at anything else except making my parents laugh when I was a kid, like singing silly songs, I am so happy that I actually did get to make a career out of it."
Mulligan: "I say exactly the same. To work consistently, to be able to make a living working as an actress is amazing. Very, very fortunate."

recentItems.title: White house Down interview, Jamie Foxx, Channing Tatum
recentItems.description:
(6 Sep 2013) 

STORYLINE:
1. SOUNDBITE (English) Channing Tatum /actor on the film
"It's obviously a serious subject of you know the White House being sort of attacked or whatever but you know we wanted it to be still a family popcorn funfair movie as well. "
(Reporter: "And you get to play the president.")
SOUNDBITE (English) Jamie Foxx/Actor: "Yes I do."
(Reporter: "Who can turn a role like that down.")
Foxx:"And be able to work with Channing Tatum. Be able work with Roland Emmerich, sometimes you just pick projects because you're going to be able to have the chance to build some good history."
2. SOUNDBITE (English) Roland Emmerich/Director on the improvising in the film
"It's a very intense story it's a hostage situation and there was already a lot of humor in the script but I have this tendency when I'm shooting a movie I'm trying to create an atmosphere where every actor can do whatever they want. We always like first shoot the script like it's written and then I say ok, now go off and improvise and add, you know your character better than I do. And there's a lot, a lot of things naturally coming out which are really really good. Some of the biggest laughs were like improvised."

recentItems.title: Rajan Singh reacts to Shilpa Shetty controversy
recentItems.description:
(12 Mar 2010) 

STORYLINE:
SHOTLIST
London, January 17th 2007
10 mins approx
1. Sit down interview with Rajan Singh, Senior Vice President, International Business, Sony Entertainment Television Asia including the following sound bites:
"Well it certainly is the talk of the country, it''s on the front pages of all the big newspapers, the Times, the Independent, the Express, everywhere, it''s also being covered by all the major news channels, so they certainly know that Big Brother is happening in the UK and the kind of reception that Shilpa has received, right from the day she went into the house, to the racism issues that are happening right now."
"A lot of the news channels are covering the clips, they''re covering the clips of crying, of how the other housemates are treating her, originally the media was covering her kind of romances with some of the male stars in the house, but it''s obviously changed now to a very much far focused approach in terms of how she''s being treated as an Indian within a very much white house."
"This was an actress who was coming from India, who was not probably been used to the kind of standards of living that we as Brit-Asians have been for 2 or 3 generations. I think that if you had a British Asian actress and actor they would have very much approached the issue of racism in the house very much different to the way Shilpa did. I think they would have taken it head on and I think that they would have told them to cut it out, and fought their ways in a more proactive and a positive way rather than not knowing how to deal with it."

recentItems.title: Man who lost sister in Gaza building collapse said she had told him debris was falling from ceiling
recentItems.description:
(16 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTIONS SUMMARY: 
++CLIENTS: EDIT HAS SHOTS OF DEAD BODIES AND SHOT OF MAN CARRYING BODY OF CHILD++

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Gaza City, Gaza Strip - 16 September 2026
1. Various of people carrying bodies of people who were killed in a collapsed building out of an ambulance and into a morgue
2. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Sherif Samoura, his sister was killed when the building collapsed:
"They could not find a tent or land, nor did they have the financial means to find housing. This was the last place they could turn to, despite the danger and their awareness that it would likely end in tragedy. A lack of resources drove them towards certain death. Just yesterday, my sister sent me a message saying that debris was falling from the ceiling—especially near the entrance. I told her to come over, that I would find a place for her, or that she could stay with me for a few days until she found somewhere else. Then, at 2 o'clock, we were shocked to learn that the house had collapsed on its occupants; we rushed to the hospital, only to find my sister dead."
3. Various of people gathering near wrapped bodies on the ground inside the morgue 
4. Man carrying the partially covered body of a killed child out of the morgue 
5. Various of people gathering outside the morgue
STORYLINE:
A damaged building in Gaza City housing about six displaced families collapsed Wednesday morning, killing at least 14 people and injuring 15. 

The 14 dead include 12 women and children, according to Zaher al-Wahidi, a spokesperson for the Gaza Health Ministry. 

The toll was expected to rise as more bodies were recovered from the wreckage.

The building had been partially destroyed in an Israeli strike earlier in the war. It was not immediately clear what caused the collapse, but in Gaza — where the majority of buildings have been damaged or destroyed — dozens of multistory structures have collapsed throughout the war, particularly during winter weather.

Building collapses have become a major hazard in Gaza. Displaced families have often returned from tent camps to homes damaged by bombardment during the almost three years of war.

recentItems.title: Controversial comedian actor releases DVD of ''Scandalous'' stand up
recentItems.description:
(12 Mar 2010) 

STORYLINE:
SHOTLIST
London, November 14th 2009
10 mins approx
1. Interview with Russell Brand including the following sound bites:
"There''s a lot of scandalous content on this particular DVD. I talk about the infamous ''Manuelgate'' scandal of last year. I talk about the VMA''s, some other material that''s quite contentious, which I think when the DVD comes out will possibly cause yet more scandal. But I''m very pleased with it. I''m very happy with it. It''s funny. It''s from when I was at the O2."
"I Don''t think she realised the impact that that would have on me because it was like, you know, there''s not a person in my life that I haven''t at some point sulked about and not spoken to for at least a few days but West Ham United, even when we went down under (Glen) Roeder, even with the bonds scheme when they tried to sell the club back to the fans, you know, there''s not been a single time when I''ve stopped supporting West Ham United. It''s a consistency. It''s like reaching back into my childhood, taking the injured nincompoop of a boy I was and sort of putting a laurel upon his brow. It was marvellous and plus she looked amazing in it so yeah, it was wicked."
"I would have done nothing differently. I think it worked out really well. I''m really happy with what I''m doing now. I''m happy with my personal life. I''m happy with my professional life. I apologised for the thing I did wrong to the person I did it wrong to. The whole subsequent scandal, as brilliantly outlined in this product, was funny. It was funny, you know. I think it''s just rhubarb. It was just rhubarb and guff."
(Reporter - "Bob Shennan, the controller of (BBC) Radio 2 said a couple of weeks ago that there was no plans for you to return to Radio 2 and last night on Twitter you said that it''s been a year, give me my job back, so would you return? Do you want to return?)
Brand - "I was mucking around. I just did it for a joke. No, I''m doing ''Arthur'' and then I''m doing like another film and then another film and doing stand up and doing things where I can do what I like, you know, so no. But I''m going to do some stuff with Noel Gallagher. We''re going to do some podcasts, me and Noel Gallagher. But we won''t do it, you know, it will be under controlled conditions."
(Reporter - "Do you ever reminisce about the even with Jonathan Ross and laugh on it now?)
Brand - "We don''t laugh about it. No, we''ve moved on. No, we don''t really talk about it."
2. SOUND UP (English) Russell Brand:
"Who is using this as an opportunity to shoplift? I definitely would because a lot of the security is distracted at a time like this so yeah, feel free." 
3. Wide shot audience
